newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt Export Bank plans share issue.
newsitem.headline: Egypt Export Bank plans share issue.

text.p: The state-dominated Export Development Bank of Egypt said on Wednesday it was planning a public share offering worth about 59 million pounds in November to raise its paid-in capital to 250 million.
Financial Director Magdi el-Moushnib told Reuters the offering would also slash the government's holding in the bank to 75 percent from the current 98.6 percent.
The state has repeatedly said it will not privatise the four main retail banks but the cabinet announced the decision to sell part of Export Development Bank in September.
Moushnib said the bank's public-sector shareholders had put in another 121 million pounds since September, on top of its original paid-in capital of 69 million.
The share offering is in line with the government's policy of privatisation, which includes reducing the state's stake in joint ventures between state banks and foreign banks.
The export bank currently has 690,000 shares that rarely trade on the stock exchange.
In calendar 1995 the Export Development Bank made a net after-tax profit of 36.052 million pounds, against 31.097 million the previous year.
